question.text: Bactericidal activity of 3 cutaneous/mucosal antiseptic solutions in the presence of interfering substances: Improvement of the NF EN 13727 European Standard?
question.context: There is no standard protocol for the evaluation of antiseptics used for skin and mucous membranes in the presence of interfering substances. Our objective was to suggest trial conditions adapted from the NF EN 13727 standard, for the evaluation of antiseptics used in gynecology and dermatology. Three antiseptic solutions were tested in vitro: a chlorhexidine-benzalkonium (CB) combination, a hexamidine-chlorhexidine-chlorocresol (HCC) combination, and povidone iodine (P). The adaptation of trial conditions to the standard involved choosing dilutions, solvent, and interfering substances. The activity of solutions was assessed on the recommended strains at concentrations of 97% (pure solution), 50%, and 10% (diluted solution), and 1%. A logarithmic reduction ≥ 5 was expected after 60seconds of contact, to meet requirements of bactericidal activity. HCC did not present any bactericidal activity except on P. aeruginosa at a concentration of 97%. P was not bactericidal on E. hirae at any concentration and on S. aureus at 97%. CB had the most homogeneous bactericidal activity with a reduction>5 log on the 4 bacterial strains at concentrations of 97%, 50% and 10%.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The clinical case describes an in vitro evaluation of three antiseptic solutions against four bacterial strains, with the goal of adapting the NF EN 13727 standard for use in gynecology and dermatology. The study found that the chlorhexidine-benzalkonium (CB) combination exhibited the most homogeneous bactericidal activity, meeting the required log reduction of ≥ 5 after 60 seconds of contact on all four bacterial strains at the 97%, 50%, and 10% concentrations. Therefore, the solutions meet the requirements of the NF EN 13727 standard.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: CB had the most homogeneous bactericidal activity with a reduction>5 log on the 4 bacterial strains at concentrations of 97%, 50% and 10%.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: The clinical case focuses on the efficacy of the antiseptic solutions against specific bacterial strains. While other factors might influence the clinical outcome, the in vitro results provide a strong indication of the solutions' ability to meet the NF EN 13727 standard.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that the chlorhexidine-benzalkonium (CB) combination antiseptic solution showed the most consistent bactericidal activity across different bacterial strains and concentrations, meeting the required 5 log reduction after 60 seconds. This makes it the most effective option among the tested solutions, especially in the presence of interfering substances, which aligns with the goal of improving the NF EN 13727 standard for antiseptic evaluation.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: CB had a reduction >5 log on 4 bacterial strains at concentrations of 97%, 50%, and 10%, indicating broad-spectrum efficacy.
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: While HCC and P showed limited activity, they were not as consistently effective as CB, making CB the best choice for clinical use.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study aimed to adapt the NF EN 13727 standard for evaluating antiseptics under real-world conditions with interfering substances. The CB solution demonstrated consistent bactericidal activity across all tested strains and concentrations, meeting the ≥5 log reduction requirement. This suggests the adapted protocol successfully improved the standard’s applicability for gynecology and dermatology. The other solutions (HCC and P) failed to meet bactericidal criteria on multiple strains, highlighting the value of the adapted protocol in identifying effective antiseptics.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: CB had the most homogeneous bactericidal activity with a reduction >5 log on all 4 bacterial strains at 97%, 50%, and 10% concentrations.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: HCC and P were ruled out as effective antiseptics under the adapted protocol due to inconsistent or absent bactericidal activity, leaving CB as the only solution meeting the standard’s requirements.

olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Differentials include whether the tested concentrations and time frame adequately reflect real-world clinical use as per the proposed standard adaptation, but the main issue is the incomplete data for required strains and conditions.
